name: Línea XYZ at Viver – Morredondo, Cerro Cruz & El Ragudo bunkers
story: Viver lay at the centre of the Línea XYZ, where the Nationalist drive down the Teruel–Sagunto road and railway was stopped in July 1938. Republican engineers used the broken terrain rather than building a continuous wall. The result was a network of trenches, shelters and bunkers covering the road and the railway pass at El Ragudo. Although the Nationalists had more men and command of the air, repeated frontal assaults here failed. The town has signposted short walks to the Morredondo trenches and the Cerro Cruz defensive position, and the official Línea XYZ project maps a route to the Ragudo bunkers (Viver–Benafer).
see: Trenches at Morredondo, fortified positions on the Cerro Cruz, and concrete bunkers and railway ruins at El Ragudo.
plan: The pin marks Viver: Morredondo, Cerro Cruz and El Ragudo are separate sites around it. Morredondo and Cerro Cruz are each about an hour's walk from the town. El Ragudo is reached along the Ojos Negros greenway or by track. The CIBAL interpretation centre in Viver is open; ask the tourist office (679 881 627, viver@touristinfo.net).
